HRA Analysis: A small but competitive field kicks off tonight for the No More Than Two Lifetime Wins pacers, where TWILIGHT STORM (6) will be looking to show her class after a handy second in the Oaks last start and should take plenty of holding out late. A DRAGON FOR JOE (4) was an impressive 10-metre winner last start and looks to be back to his best after showing plenty of promise early in his career. Expect him to be right in the finish again. TAPPY (1) gets his chance from the pole draw after competing in some fairly strong company of late, including the Derby last start, and should appreciate the drop in grade. OMYBACNKNEES JUDGE (2) is a consistent pacer and looks the likely early leader, which should give him every opportunity again after a solid placing last start. WINNING BREW (3) and MY FATAL CHARM (5) would need to improve on their recent performances to be fighting out the finish, with the other four looking the main chances. Selections: TWILIGHT STORM (6), A DRAGON FOR JOE (4), TAPPY (1), OMYBACNKNEES JUDGE (2)

The open-class event of the night over the short mile brings together another small field, but it should still be a truly run affair. WAVES OF CHANCE (1) will again be looking to lead from start to finish, as he did four starts ago when winning in fast time. He disappointed when leading two starts back before over-racing due to gear issues last start, but at his best he could take plenty of running down. GO THE RED (3) added another victory to his record after being extremely consistent since arriving in the state and again looks a major player. BETTABLACK TIGER (2) arguably possesses the most talent in the field at his best, although he may be better suited over a longer trip. A genuinely run mile would enhance his chances, noting he has also undergone a stable change since his previous start. KEAYANG FITZY (4), WATERMELON SUGAR (5) and MAEBEE (6) will need to improve on their recent performances to beat the favoured runners, but could sneak into the placings if those ahead of them overdo things throughout. Selections: GO THE RED (3), BETTABLACK TIGER (2), WAVES OF CHANCE (1), WATERMELON SUGAR (5)

An even front row makes the speed map difficult to assess, with plenty of gate speed engaged and the early stages capable of playing out a number of different ways. ATOMIC BLACK (2) continues to work his way through the grades and get the job done, producing another strong victory last start despite copping interference early. PHOTO FIRST (3) battled on nicely for third when first up from a break and should take good improvement from that performance. CUZZY BRO (5), IRON CLAD (6) and ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (8) are always around the mark in these types of races and regularly find their way into the placings. SMOOTH REASON (4) has been thereabouts in features company of late and could be the one at odds if she brings her best form. POWER UP (7) did plenty of work early before fading over the longer distance last start and should appreciate coming back to this grade and being driven with a sit, although she will be relying on genuine tempo to bring her into the race late. CENTURIAN MISS (1) rises in class but is favoured by the pole draw. Selections: ATOMIC BLACK (2), PHOTO FIRST (3), POWER UP (7), CUZZY BRO (5)

The standing-start event brings together another even affair, where TULLAH GIRL (1) and SAPPHIRE GAMBLER (2) are normally the two best beginners from the front line and will be looking to make the most of their favourable handicaps again here. SPOOKY GIRL (5) pinged away from the tapes last start and was able to roll along at even quarters, although she does rise in grade here. ZEUS IMMORTAL (3) and HAMMER DAN (4) are consistent pacers who should be right in the finish if able to find positions on speed with cover. WILL HE PIKE (8) looks the best chance of the 10-metre runners and will again be relying on a nice run in transit and a good drive to allow him to finish off strongly. Selections: TULLAH GIRL (1), ZEUS IMMORTAL (3), WILL HE PIKE (8), HAMMER DAN (4)

Looks to be plenty of gate speed across the front row over the short distance in a race where it wouldn't surprise to see any runner pop up and win. MISS COLLANN (1) gets her chance to return to form after some fair efforts of late and should appreciate getting back to the short trip from the pole draw. Expect INTO THE HARKNESS (2) and MY WAY (3) to also push out early in search of the front or a position on speed, while MISTA EAGLE (7) could be lit up from the wide gate over his pet trip and give a sight at odds. JOHN VINCENT (5) was a clear black booker last start after making excellent ground from the back of the field in sharp time. Expect he may again be saved for one run, although he does strike an awkward draw. MUZZAME MATE (11) looks the best of the back-row chances, but it is always difficult to win from there over the short distance unless they go silly up front. GOODTIME OSCAR (8) could be the one at odds from a soft pegs draw if the gaps appear late. Selections: MISS COLLANN (1), JOHN VINCENT (5), MUZZAME MATE (11), GOODTIME OSCAR (7)

MIGHT AND TEMERITY (2) again uses the double claim to gain entry into this field and should be looking to be the first runner to the pegs over the 1680-metre trip after an okay third in slightly stronger company last start. KEAYANG LEXI (1) again draws the pole and has been thereabouts in races of this nature, so should get every opportunity from the draw. THE DEVILS FLAME (4) has been super consistent since arriving on the island and should appreciate the drop in class. However, the awkward draw may see him doing some work early and throughout, but he certainly can't be ruled out. LIKEABLE ROGUE (9) gets a nice trailing draw and continues to knock on the door for another victory. The veterans JEREMY WELLS (10) and KENYA (11) both come off last-start victories and will be dangerous again, although they will be relying on genuine tempo throughout to allow them to finish home strongly over the short distance from their awkward draws. Selections: MIGHT AND TEMERITY (2), THE DEVILS FLAME (4), LIKEABLE ROGUE (9), KENYA (11)

The second of the No More Than Two Wins events, where CRAYONS TO PERFUME (2) looks the best bet of the night following two strong performances since arriving in the state. Expect her to push forward from the draw, find the front and prove too strong for this opposition. JILLSTIGER (5) wasn't far away in the Oaks last start and arguably should have won her start prior with more luck in running, so looks the obvious danger if things fall her way in transit. WEE GEORGIE WOOD (8) again draws awkwardly on the back row but continues to race well, while it wouldn't surprise to see POST KEG (9) pop up and win if he brings his best form from a nice trailing draw behind the expected favourite. ALL ABOUT SADIE (6) continues to fill the placings in races of this grade and should again be running home strongly with a favourable run in transit. Selections: CRAYONS TO PERFUME (2), JILLSTIGER (5), POST KEG (9), WEE GEORGIE WOOD (8)

SHEMEANSBUSINESS (2) won nicely in fast time over the short distance two starts back and will be looking to replicate that performance here after a competitive fourth in the Oaks last start. Expect she may cop some early pressure from SHADES OF SILK (4), who possesses good gate speed and could ensure a solid tempo throughout. He clearly has ability when at his best. JUST LIKA DREAM (5) resumes from a spell after putting together some handy performances previously, although she strikes an awkward draw first up over the short distance. ROCKY STRIDE (8) is a handy three-year-old who has been competing in stronger company of late. He draws awkwardly but should be right in the finish with any luck in running. DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (9) is always earning cheques for connections and somewhat drops back in grade here. He gets his chance from a favourable trailing draw behind the expected leader. JET TO HEAVEN (1) broke on the first corner when fancied in the market last start but has produced some nice performances throughout his career and can be in the finish if he brings his best behaviour. Selections: SHEMEANSBUSINESS (2), ROCKY STRIDE (8), DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (9), JET TO HEAVEN (1)

ART HUNTSMAN (2) broke through for a well-deserved victory two starts back when leading throughout in good time over the mile, before being scratched at the start last time after running into interference in the score-up. He may cop some early pressure from WEONA EAGLE (5), who returned to her best form last start and possesses dazzling gate speed. LETSGOBRO (7) is another sharp beginner and finally broke through last start following a long run of outs, so there could be some genuine speed on early. MOVESLIKEALADY (8) can never be left out in these sorts of races and should be sneaking through the gaps late, as she usually does. LAID BACK (9) has been producing strong performances throughout this preparation and continues to threaten to break through, only to keep finding one better. He should get another good opportunity to return to the winner's circle here. Selections: LAID BACK (9), WEONA EAGLE (5), MOVESLIKEALADY (8), ART HUNTSMAN (2)

The low-class race of the night, where trainer Wayne Yole holds the key to the speed map with his three well-drawn runners all capable of showing good speed early. QUEENOFDANCE (1) won at big odds last start over her preferred mile distance, so it wouldn't surprise to see her take a sit on FEELINKINDALUCKY (2) rather than engage in an early battle. BARBETTE (3) has loomed as the winner a few times of late without getting the job done and gets another nice run in transit here from the handy draw. TALK IS CHEAP (7) resumes from a let-up and could be the runner that has a crack for the front early, despite drawing out wide. The veteran GOBSMACKED (8) will again be looking to finish strongly from the back row, while ROSE NOIRE (6) will be relying on genuine early tempo to bring her into the race late. Selections: FEELINKINDALUCKY (2), GOBSMACKED (8), BARBETTE (3), TALK IS CHEAP (7) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:NOTGUILTY (3) is resuming since a seventh at Bendigo back in November. His two starts were in a heat of the Breeders Challenge and in a heat of the Super Series so he met strong opposition and his trial form in South Australia has been sound. He should give a bold showing first up. BETTER THEN DAICOS (6) met stronger opposition when fourth behind Fantasy Flight at Melton, where he led out then took cover. This looks to be a more suitable assignment so an improved effort is expected. NO GOOD REASON (2) is a maiden from 11 starts but all of his five placed efforts have been over the sprint distance so he should be prominent throughout under these conditions. LAMBRO BUOY (1) is perfectly drawn for his Mildura debut and is a minor place chance. BACK: NOTGUILTY (3) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: NOTGUILTY (3), BETTER THAN DAICOS (6), NO GOOD REASON (2), LAMBRO BUOY (1)

OVERVIEW:SEASIDE LADY (7) ran a cracking race for second behind Royal Rockstar at Ballarat last outing. She has since transferred to astute South Australian mentor Ryan Hryhorec and she meets a very suitable assignment for her Mildura debut so she will prove very hard to beat. CAPTIVATE ME (1) attempted to lead throughout when he copped plenty of pressure in the back straight on the final occasion and battled on well for second behind You’ve Been Served last week. He is perfectly drawn over the sprint distance and is capable of going one better now. ALMIGHTY RUSH (3) has performed consistently in three starts to date and is worth a ticket each way. She raced without cover and battled on well for fourth behind The Ninja last outing. CRUEL MISTRESS (5) trailed the leader and battled on fairly well for third in the race won by You’ve Been Served last week. She has been placed at her past three starts and is a place chance again. BACK: SEASIDE LADY (7) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: SEASIDE LADY (7), CAPTIVATE ME (1), ALMIGHTY RUSH (3), CRUEL MISTRESS (5)

OVERVIEW: KYORETSU (1) is a fast beginner and should take catching from the pole position. He was aggressively driven from the outside of the second row to get up without cover when he won three starts ago and will appreciate his best draw for some time. SPORTSBOU (6) is poorly drawn but appears to be well placed against this line up. She finished off best from midfield when she scored at Mildura three starts ago and she met a strong field at her latest unplaced effort behind Savon De Roche. THE GOLDEN HOOK (8) makes his debut for trainer Naomi Kerr and his form in the South-East has been sound. He is capable of sprinting to the line quickly with the right trail forward and should be competitive at his first local attempt. UNITED (9) tends to race best when he is close to the speed so being drawn on the second line is a disadvantage. He has been doing a lot of his racing against the open grade at Mildura so this appears to be a suitable assignment. SELECTIONS: KYORETSU (1), SPORTSBOU (6), THE GOLDEN HOOK (8), UNITED (9)

OVERVIEW: It is a strong field with several winning chances. LETSGO BIG GIRL (5) will appreciate the move to the front line and performs best over the sprint distance. She commenced on the inside of the second row and was badly blocked for a run when an unlucky fifth behind GUEST ARTIST (3) last week. She appears to be a good value hope. GUEST ARTIST (3) led throughout and scored under similar conditions last week. That was his best effort since coming from New South Wales and a repeat performance will see him going close again. WIPEOUT (9) produced his best run for some time when he was driven aggressively to find the lead and fought on strongly at Mildura last outing. He drops back to the second line now but is worth thought again. CEMETERY BAY (8) has been racing well against the open class at Mildura and will find this race to be slightly easier. He is worth thought along with the South Australian pacer MISS OUT (4). SELECTIONS: LETSGO BIG GIRL (5), GUEST ARTIST (3), WIPEOUT (9), CEMETERY BAY (8)

OVERVIEW:BOHEMIAN BRAIDS (2) is a South Australian trained pacer that boasts good gate speed and excels over the sprint distance. He led throughout at a Globe Derby victory three starts ago and raced fiercely in the front running role at his latest fourth in a handy mile rate of 1.58.2. He should give a bold showing over the short trip. HESASTAR (1) pressed forward to race without cover and battled on strongly for second behind CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (8) last week. He performs best when he is close to the speed so he is perfectly drawn to suit his racing pattern. SNEAKY PHILTRA (7) finished off reasonably well for fourth last week. Her form prior was sound and she was a runaway winner at Mildura on July 31 so she must be respected. ACCELERE (6) appeared to have his chance at his Mildura return last week but he was heavily supported ($1-45fav!) and he performed well at the trials prior so he cannot be dismissed. BACK: BOHEMIAN BRAIDS (2) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: BOHEMIAN BRAIDS (2), HESASTAR (1), SNEAKY PHILTRA (7), ACCELERE (6)

OVERVIEW: MAJOR LINCOLN (9) commenced from the inside of the second line, settled three back on the markers and was caught behind tiring horses before storming home to win impressively at Mildura last week. This is a field of similar standard and he should prove hard to hold out again. KEAYANG CRIPPA (5) pushed forward to race without cover, took on the leader a long way from home and drew clear on the home turn before being run down by MAJOR LINCOLN (9) last week. His effort was sound and he looms as a strong winning chance again. FLEUR BELLA (6) is a former New South Wales pacer, which joins trainer Naomi Kerr. She is yet to win in 11 starts for the season but she did post a mile rate of 1.53.7 when she scored at Newcastle in July 2025 so she would be highly competitive at her best form. EGBERT (4) finished off well when a close second behind PUNTO CALIENTE (8) two starts ago and has claims from his reasonable draw. SELECTIONS: MAJOR LINCOLN (9), KEAYANG CRIPPA (5), FLEUR BELLA (6), EGBERT (4)

OVERVIEW: CELESTIAL NEBULAE (11) came from a rearward position and produced a powerful finishing burst when a big winner at Charlton last outing. That was his second run back from a long spell and he should continue to improve with race fitness so he must be respected. LISTEN TO THE HAND (8) led throughout at a Mildura victory when resuming since August 2025 then followed with a close up fourth at Swan Hill. He joins trainer Naomi Kerr and looms as one of the leading chances again. BERSAGLIERE (7) was resuming since November when second at Gawler. He should strip fitter from that performance and boasts a consistent record so he cannot be dismissed. MY BELLA (1) ran a sharper race at her second run back from a break and is perfectly drawn so she is not without a chance. SELECTIONS: CELESTIAL NEBULAE (11), LISTEN TO THE HAND (8), BERSAGLIERE (7), MY BELLA (1)

OVERVIEW: VINNY ROCK (11) is a versatile pacer, which has performed well at Mildura previously and maintains a consistent form line. He finished fourth behind the smart pacer Co Captain at Ballarat last outing and is capable of overcoming the extreme draw. CAULONIA TERROR (7) was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished off strongly for an eye-catching third behind Just Incredible last week. He has done well since dropping back into a workable class and should be finishing off strongly again. ROYAL ROCKSTAR (5) was able to find the lead shortly after the start and held off his rivals to win at Ballarat on August 05. He broke stride when looking to find a forward position shortly after the start and lost his chance last week. He should be competitive under these conditions if he delivers a fool proof display. WHITEHAVEN BEACH (1) and RUBBLEONTHEDOUBLE (10) are both capable of showing up without surprising. BACK: VINNY ROCK (11) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: VINNY ROCK (11), CAULONIA TERROR (7), ROYAL ROCKSTAR (5), WHITEHAVEN BEACH (1)

OVERVIEW: LENARD ESS (9) is a real stable favourite of trainer Jess Tubbs and he landed a 19th career win at Melton last Friday when driven perfectly by James Herbertson. He led, handed up and then sprint-landed to a powerful victory as a short-priced favourite. He had gate one there, and while he won’t find the fence this time, he looks good enough to go close in what shapes as a very similar event. ALLHEARTNOHEIGHT (3) is flying for trainer Brett Cole and came from off speed to land his second-straight victory in slightly easier grade last Friday. He’s stepping up a shade in class here, but must be regarded as a winning chance based on his current form. Stablemate GOODTIME MAE (2) got home well from back in the field from a horror draw to finish fifth in the same race and draws to settle much closer this time, while WICHITA KANSAS (5) was a winner two starts back here at Melton and ran soundly for fourth behind LENARD ESS (9) last time. He’s some chance along with FREAK OUT (7) and WOODLEA DIEGO (4), who would need luck but are capable. BACK: LENARD ESS (9) – 1 unit (win) SELECTIONS: LENARD ESS (9), ALLHEARTNOHEIGHT (3), GOODTIME MAE (2), WICHITA KANSAS (5)

OVERVIEW: SMACK BANG BART (6) won a qualifier and final of the rich Nutrien series to start his career and then tackled the Group 1 Protostar slot race in Queensland, where he finished down the track as an $8 chance. He was beaten as a short-priced favourite by the handy Boystrous at Wagga following a month away from the races on August 19, but looks very handy and is the horse to beat in this opening heat of the Vicbred Super Series for two-year-old colts and geldings. LETITRIDELUV (3) won smartly on debut when running down a handy one in La Cantatrice and then closed well for second before a break. He’s trialled up nicely with wins at Melton and Geelong ahead of this first-up assignment and should run well. FULLY RECKLESS (2) has victories at Mildura and Wagga to his name from three career outings and also trialled nicely at Shepparton recently, while SOHO CRUZA (5), who hails from the powerful Michael Stanley stable, and ALLOA (4), who won on debut at Kilmore, should also be respected. SELECTIONS: SMACK BANG BART (6), LETITRIDELUV (3), FULLY RECKLESS (2), SOHO CRUZA (5)

OVERVIEW: SOME HIGH (5) might have the gate speed and barrier draw to cross to the fence and lead this assignment, which could be the winning move. He led, handed up and just couldn’t reel in stablemate Cardigan Sniper at Melton latest, which followed a front-running win at Melton and solid third placing in the hot Rising Star feature at Ballarat. Not sure he’s a star, but he might get the right run to pinch this Vicbred heat. KINGS GALLERY (7) is a very handy customer from the Chris Svanosio stable who has backed up his four successive runner-up placings to Emma Stewart rivals with two dominant wins since returning from a break. From a better gate I’d probably have him on top, but seven makes it tricky. SOHO BELLAGIO (6) won his debut start at Menangle as a short-priced favourite by a huge 24.7m margin in impressive style and he looks well and truly above average, while the honest and experienced BAYSTYLE (3), CRIPPA (8) and first-starter KELROSE CULLEN (4) might not be major winning hopes but are others to consider for wider exotics. SELECTIONS: SOME HIGH (5), KINGS GALLERY (7), SOHO BELLAGIO (6), BAYSTYLE (3)

OVERVIEW: CARDIGAN SNIPER (3) looks set to run a short-priced elect after a great start to his career which has included feature wins in the rich APG final and Youthful Stakes last time out at Melton. There, he was able to work to the front and win despite some wayward manners. You’d anticipate that he finds the top again, and from there he’s the horse to beat. LAKE COMO (4) chased him home for third in the Youthful Stakes in what was a brave effort off the pegs and his debut win from three back the fence at Maryborough was brilliant. He’s a nice type and key danger, as is CARDIGAN SNIPER’S (3) stablemate AUSTON (7), who won by panels on debut at Hobart before being run down late at Launceston. A big watch first-up in Victoria. STERLING GIGI (1) broke his maiden in good style last week at Kilmore following a nice second to the smart Kings Gallery and he can figure from the good draw. SELECTIONS: CARDIGAN SNIPER (3), LAKE COMO (4), AUSTON (7), STERLING GIGI (1)

OVERVIEW: Cracking start to the Vicbred Super Series for the two-year-old fillies, with a number of horses bringing in great form. SOHO ASTER (1) won a heat of the Gold Tiara before placing second in the Group 1 final, and returned from a freshen with a narrow victory at Menangle on August 18. She has good gate speed, a pole draw and might be the horse to beat from the front. DECOUPAGE (7) also brings impressive New South Wales form to Victoria. She was second on debut in the Pink Bonnet Stakes at Menangle in May and ran a great second in the $200,000 Nutrien series final at Wagga later that month before breaking her maiden first-up last Friday at Newcastle by a whopping 18.4m. She looks a key contender, as does TEERDEE (5) who is returning from a spell. She closed her last campaign with a midfield placing (after coming from a mile back at the bell) in the Nutrien final and ran a number of good races despite tough trips before that. DREAMS FOREVER (6), who failed after a tough run as favourite on debut at Maryborough on August 3, and LA CANTATRICE (2), who was very impressive winning the Youthful Stakes at Melton on August 15, are the other fancies. SELECTIONS: SOHO ASTER (1), DECOUPAGE (7), TEERDEE (5), LA CANTATRICE (2)

OVERVIEW: IDEAL FRANKIE (4) stamped herself as a star of her age group with massive 21.8m, 46.9m and 42.6m wins in her first three race starts, which included victory in the rich APG series at Melton in late June. That earned her a place in the Group 1 Protostar slot race at Albion Park, where she ultimately failed and finished towards the back of the field. She’s been freshened and looks clearly the horse to beat. SOHO SPARKLE (2) galloped out of play as favourite in a heat of the Gold Tiara on debut in March and heads here on the back of a good second placing at the Menangle trials recently, while SHES CAPTIVATING (3) won a trial at Ballarat over HEAVENLY GEM (6) on August 19 but there was no vision of that hit-out so it’s hard to weigh up the performances. CARTIMANDUA (5) wasn’t overly fancied by punters on debut at Shepparton, but ran well for third and can be included for the back end of trifectas and First 4s. SELECTIONS: IDEAL FRANKIE (4), SOHO SPARKLE (2), SHES CAPTIVATING (3), HEAVENLY GEM (6)

OVERVIEW: KAHULA (1) will start a very warm favourite here for Emma Stewart and Mark Pitt from the barrier one draw. Her form lines are outstanding from four career starts, including a dominant victory in the $200,000 Nutrien series final in May and a great third, beaten just a head, in the Group 1 Protostar at Albion Park in July. Her gate speed is a little query, but she should ultimately end up in front and prove too classy. ONELOOK (2) appeared the winner of the Youthful Stakes at Melton on August 15, and despite being worn down late by La Cantatrice, it was a great effort. She’s a leading contender for second place, alongside New South Wales visitor LATHER ME UP (7), who is first-up following a closing third in the Group 1 Gold Tiara, and MY ROCKING HORSE (8), who has run two good second placings – beating home ONELOOK (2) on one occasion – to start her career. SELECTIONS: KAHULA (1), ONELOOK (2), LATHER ME UP (7), MY ROCKING HORSE (8)

OVERVIEW: MAJESTIC MONARCH (8) caught the eye with a good third behind BUSLIN BRODY (5) first-up after more than a year away from the races at Kilmore on August 13, then was backed off the map before leading and turning the tables on that horse with a dominant victory at the same track last week. Harder here from the back row, but he looks very tough to hold out based off that recent effort. The old boy BUSLIN BRODY (5) is in great form and has obvious claims given he beat the on-top selection and ran well from the back of the field subsequent to that, SHAQ THE ANVIL (2) led and defeated Joe Lou in easier grade at Ballarat last week and that horse has won again since, and while STRAIGHT TO THETOP (4) was a little disappointing from behind the leader at Shepparton on Tuesday, she was only beaten by a neck to BUSLIN BRODY (5) in that recent race and had won prior to that. She looks a chance of finding the front and would be a major player if she found it. BACK: MAJESTIC MONARCH (8) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: MAJESTIC MONARCH (8), BUSLIN BRODY (5), SHAQ THE ANVIL (2), STRAIGHT TO THETOP (4)

OVERVIEW: SWEET FLORABEL (7) was well fancied on debut at Melton last Friday night, and while not much went right for her, she ran a cracking race for third. She galloped at the start and lost significant ground, chased hard to settle last and was forced wide down the back straight when making her run. She did a great job to only be beaten around 8m by Fantasy Flight and Sweetsugarcandyman, who have both shown good potential. Confident she gets the job done here in a very suitable maiden. DIAMOND CHIPP (2) has hit the line well in all three career starts from back in the field to be beaten less than 10m on each occasion and draws well here, SMOKEN HEAVEN (4) hasn’t beaten a runner home his past two but did manage a close-up third to Farroh Joe before that, while ROBLEN DEMON (5) produced a career-best second placing last start at Geelong but did find the pegs there and it might not be the case from gate five this time around. BACK: SWEET FLORABEL (7) – 7 units (win) SELECTIONS: SWEET FLORABEL (7), DIAMOND CHIPP (2), SMOKEN HEAVEN (4), ROBLEN DEMON (5) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R1 #9 LENARD ESS – 1 unit (win) R8 #8 MAJESTIC MONARCH – 2 units (win) R9 #7 SWEET FLORABEL – 7 units (win) EARLY QUADDIE 2,3,4,5,7,9/2,3,6/5,6,7/3 QUADDIE 1,2,5,6,7/4/1/2,4,5,8 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW: Ripper race to start proceedings at HQ where the New Zealand import WORDS (10) looks to get a great chance. His first-up run here on our shores was a cracker when he speared to the front, ran strong sections and bolted in for an 8.8m victory over ZENARIO (6). He was then very competitive when only beaten 4.3m into third by Fairplay at Melton last time and there looks enough tempo – with SOHO DARKNSTORMY (5) likely to fly the arm and keep running – for him to work into this race off the back row. MISS ARI (3) is a wonderfully talented mare who was perhaps a shade disappointing when only fourth last start, but all her prior form is outstanding, HITTHEROADJACK (1) gets the good gate, and while he lacks point-to-point speed, he’s a real trier and hasn’t been beaten far in his runs since a Melton victory over last weekend’s winner PESCI (11), who is another with a good hope alongside stablemate ZENARIO (6), who has been runner-up his past two and like GOOD TOBE LOCKSLEY (7), ATA RANGI (9) and SOAP AND BUBBLES (12), just needs the right trip to strike. SELECTIONS: WORDS (10), MISS ARI (3), HITTHEROADJACK (1), ZENARIO (6)

OVERVIEW: THE NAKED ART (9) worked to the chair and sat parked to win a heat of a NMW series here on August 15 in what was a brilliant display, and then had her chances cruelled by a bad gate in the final yet still managed to close hard for fourth behind The Last Trip. She’s been flying for a some time now and looks poised to run another big race from the nice trailing draw. HIGHLANDHARTBREAKA (10) landed the one-one and wore down his stablemate to win over 1200m last Friday night and is a handy type who is often running home soundly, LOUGLE (12) was brilliant coming from the back of the field for third behind THE NAKED ART (9) in that aforementioned heat and backed it up with another close-up third from the front in the final, while TALERN LOFTY (1) draws to hold the front if David Miles desires and can give a sight over the 1720m. Others wouldn’t shock, including KING SAINT (4), SAVON DE ROCHE (5) and ROYAL APPOINTMENT (11). BACK: THE NAKED ART (9) – 1 unit (win) SELECTIONS: THE NAKED ART (9), HIGHLANDHARTBREAKA (10), LOUGLE (12), TALERN LOFTY (1)

OVERVIEW: BULLETPROOF BOY (9) was first-up from a break without a trial and had the extreme back row draw last weekend in a hot free-for-all at Melton, but he ran really well to grab third. He was beaten 10.8m in the end, but it was a great effort given all those circumstances and this looks a shade easier from a better gate with some added fitness on his side. The one they have to beat. CALEXICO (1) finished seventh in that same race last Saturday from three back the pegs, but maps to hold the front here and could certainly run an improved race if he was able to control things at the top. MY ULTIMATE BARNEY (8) is first-up from a big Bendigo win in easier company on July 1 and is a very talented pacer, while the veteran TRIPLE EIGHT (6) rarely wins these days but is hard to discount as he’s a powerful finisher and is always one to consider for trifectas and First 4s. SELECTIONS: BULLETPROOF BOY (9), CALEXICO (1), MY ULTIMATE BARNEY (8), TRIPLE EIGHT (6)

OVERVIEW: FARROKH (10) is flying at the moment for Chris Lang and Sonia Mahar, with an eye-catching third in stronger grade than this last weekend behind Ijustcalledtosay and another great effort from last for fifth behind SKY FLAIR (8) back on August 1. He beat a few of these rivals when he last won at Kilmore and I fancy he’s the testing material once again. SKY FLAIR (8) has been brilliant this campaign and made it back-to-back victories when she sprinted over the top from the running line to score on August 15, DISTANT SUN (3) was a touch disappointing last start when fancied behind Kyvalley Michael but the two runs prior were very good efforts at Kilmore, and CENTURION DREAM (2) can improve on last weekend’s effort where she was clearly outclassed and should be able to cross the honest SAMMY HALLER (1), who is some chance along with a few others like KARBINE (6) and ALDEBARAN SUE (11). BACK: FARROKH (10) – 1 unit (each-way) SELECTIONS: FARROKH (10), SKY FLAIR (8), DISTANT SUN (3), CENTURION DREAM (2)

OVERVIEW: THUNDERFIRE (8) had every reason to be beaten first-up from a spell at Cranbourne on August 16 when caught parked, but dug deep and scored a tough victory in a sizzling 55.9 last half. It was the performance of a very talented pacer, who boasts a career record of four wins from seven starts. He should be fitter for that run and looks a good chance of landing leader’s back here over the 1720m trip with pole-marker SCOOTER LOU (1) a likely front-runner. With even luck, he looks very hard to beat. EVILEYE (3) was so brave from the chair last time when third behind The Final Dance and she’s going much better than her numerical form would suggest, MONTANA PRIDE (6) had a softer run in transit and charged late for second in that same race and all his recent form is good, while MITZI SAID (10) is first-up from a break and trialled nicely for second in decent time at Kilmore recently. She was very competitive in higher-graded races than this last campaign and is a genuine contender with the right tempo. BACK: THUNDERFIRE (8) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: THUNDERFIRE (8), EVILEYE (3), MITZI SAID (10), MONTANA PRIDE (6)

OVERVIEW: Very tricky race to work out, but KYVALLEY MICHAEL (10) is going really well and broke through for a big win in easier grade last Friday at Melton when he was able to roll around and find the front. He’d run a number of other good races prior to that, and with the expected solid tempo here, he can be a major factor late. SPIRITED LASS (1) was caught parked and dropped out late in her bid for three-straight wins last time at Melton but can improve sharply from gate one, ARTIGAS (8) won a recent trial at Maryborough ahead of this assignment and did score well three times in-a-row before a freshen, while the consistent ROCKY VALLEY (6), the first-up CLAUDYS HERO (7) and fast-starting pair ALDEBARAN SUSANNE (4) and PROHIBITED GRACE (3) headline the others that can threaten with the right luck. Wide Quaddie leg! SELECTIONS: KYVALLEY MICHAEL (10), SPIRITED LASS (1), ARTIGAS (8), ROCKY VALLEY (6)

OVERVIEW: DRESSED IN GOLD (10) brings strong formlines to this race, with a good third to the talented Lambro Mach last time despite being parked and a front-running second in a similar 0W/15.0K stake event when nailed late by Keayang Payton with a good margin back to third. He’s narrowly fancied in a wide-open race where there’s a few key winning chances. ROCKELLA (8) sat parked for the last lap and did a great job to win narrowly in a slick 55.9 last half at Ballarat on August 19, KATUNGA EXPRESS (7) charged late to only be beaten 3.8m at Wagga last week and hit the line similarly well at Melton when third prior to that, while BETTOR PUNTER (4) looks pretty progressive and backed up his good wins at Cranbourne and Melton with strong placings at Kilmore and Ballarat. SELECTIONS: DRESSED IN GOLD (10), ROCKELLA (8), KATUNGA EXPRESS (7), BETTOR PUNTER (4)

OVERVIEW: OLLIES THE BOSS (2) has been all around the winner’s stall this campaign without setting foot in it, and if he’s able to work to the front here over the 1720m, he gets a good chance to break through. He’s run six placings from seven starts this preparation and heads into this race on the back of a 5.1m defeat in a strong race at Melton last Saturday night. FIRE MARSHALL (1) didn’t do much first-up from a break here at Melton on August 21, but barrier one makes his life much easier and he ran some good races last campaign. EYE WISH (3) won the rich Nutrien series final for three-year-old fillies in late May and heads here first-up from a freshen. She also placed third in a Group 2 Gold Bracelet during March and is very classy, but this is a step-up against seasoned horses and the opposite sex. IMA TERMINATOR (8) is going along okay and is among a few others that could prevail with the right trip such as KOSIMO (9), CLYMENUS (10) and impressive first-up Charlton winner CAPTAIN PINS (6). SELECTIONS: OLLIES THE BOSS (2), FIRE MARSHALL (1), EYE WISH (3), IMA TERMINATOR (8)

OVERVIEW: Feature race for the up-to-55 mares and Luke Sutherland gets a great chance with a horse he owns and drives, MILOLA ROCK (3). Her three runs for trainer Aaron Dunn were all really good, including a dominant win at Maryborough when she surged clear to score by 7.7m. She didn’t have a great deal of clear air last time at Charlton but was still only beaten 8.1m, and now joins the Tori Hutchins barn. Confident she runs well and goes close here. DELIGHTFUL MIKI (8) has been beaten as a red-hot favourite her last two when leading at Maryborough and Kilmore but is right in this back to her best, HUXHAM CHUBB (4) led and controlled things for an easy win at Charlton two back and might be one to fly the arm and find the front, while MISS ADDI (5) is lightly raced and managed a brave second from the chair first-up at Cranbourne on August 16. There’s definite ability there. BACK: MILOLA ROCK (3) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: MILOLA ROCK (3), DELIGHTFUL MIKI (8), HUXHAM CHUBB (4), MISS ADDI (5)

OVERVIEW: FOUROUTOFFIVE (5) doesn’t win out of turn, but he’s run some really good races this campaign against strong opposition and might represent the value here in the last of 10. He was caught parked and still ran second to the flying Alrighty his last two, and produced solid efforts for third behind free-for-all class trotters Hoppy and Gatesys Gem prior to that. This looks his type of contest. QUIRKY CHARACTER (4) has been back to the trials since a string of plain efforts and is certainly a major winning hope at his best, IJUSTCALLEDTOSAY (6) claimed his third win this campaign coming from off speed to run down ALDEBARAN ABEL (1) last week and can score again, while DICHOTOMY (7) chased hard for third after galloping early last week behind I Am Wilma and actually did well to get so close. She’s talented on her day and wouldn’t shock. BACK: FOUROUTOFFIVE (5) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: FOUROUTOFFIVE (5), QUIRKY CHARACTER (4), IJUSTCALLEDTOSAY (6), ALDEBARAN ABEL (1) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R2 #9 THE NAKED ART – 1 unit (win) R4 #10 FARROKH – 1 unit (each-way) R5 #8 THUNDERFIRE – 2 units (win) R9 #3 MILOLA ROCK – 3 units (win) R10 #5 FOUROUTOFFIVE – 2 units (win) EARLY QUADDIE 1,3,6,7,9,10/1,5,9,10,11,12/1,8,9/3,8,10 QUADDIE 3,8,10/1,4,6,8,10/4,7,8,10/1,2,3,8,9 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

CAPTAIN JAZZ (6) secured a good run last time out and just couldn’t quite run down Crippa Max in a race they ran a very slick last half. She draws poorly but does have good tactical speed and should be very hard to hold out. QUIK CHANGE (1) has good gate speed and should be able to drive through and lead before having options from there. He was very good getting back in the run and finishing strongly last time out at Albion Park behind Mister Reactor. ZAC DANIELS (2) was very good recently when leading at this track and being taken on throughout before not being beaten far. If he was able to work to the lead in the early stages he would likely be hard to run down in this race. MISS SYRAH (3) was a winner three starts ago when securing a good run up on speed before dashing up nicely. She should secure a good run in this race and can be running on late again. SELECTIONS: CAPAIN JAZZ (6), QUIK CHANGE (1), ZAC DANIELS (2), MISS SYRAH (3), SUGGESTED BET: CAPTAIN JAZZ (6) to win.

BLING THE NOISE (5) was a nice winner in a recent race two starts ago at this track when leading all the way. He finds a race where he may be able to press forward and find a prominent position. ASCOT ANNIE (1) should secure a good run from the perfect draw in this race. Her latest win came at this track when securing the perfect leading back trail and was able to prove too good there. TELLMEABOUTIT (10) was forced to race without cover last time out and was able to score a good win there beating Little Whippet at this track and rating good time. He should be able to secure a similar type of run in this race and should be hard to beat. WELL SAID NUGGET (7) secured a good run last time out and was running on strongly behind Arkuna. He should get a good run in this race and if the gaps appear at the right time he should be hard to beat. SELECTIONS: BLING THE NOISE (5), ASCOT ANNIE (1), TELLMEABOUTIT (10), WELL SAID NUGGET (7) SUGGESTED BET: WELL SAID NUGGET (7) to win.

GOOD WORD THAT (3) doesn’t have brilliant early speed but may be able to work forward and find the front. She ran well in a race taken out by Jay Tee Tyron last start at Albion Park when finishing fifth. EBONY BELLE (5) has good early speed and may look for a prominent position in the early stages of this race. She was shuffled back last start and couldn’t get into the race there which was taken out by Ideal Tiger. MADAM WEST (9) was running on strongly two starts ago and just couldn’t quite reel in Bokhari there at this track. She should get a good run off the speed again and can be running on late. PLAYING FOR KEEPS (10) was able to secure a good run off the speed and made up some ground late behind Three Machs at this track. She has been racing well and could be suited if there is early tempo. SELECTIONS: GOOD WORD THAT (3),EBONY BELLE (5), MADAM WEST (9), PLAYING FOR KEEPS (10) SUGGESTED BET: GOOD WORD THAT (3) to win.

JAY TEE TYRON (8) led from a wide draw last time out and was able to prove too good there leading all the way. He should get a good run off the speed this time in this race and looks well placed again in this field. THE HARRIS HAWK (9) drew poorly last time out and was running on well into fourth. He should get a good run off the speed and will be running on strongly late if the race is run to suit. FAVREAU (5) has been excellent recently winning two starts ago after doing the work before just coming up short last time out running second. He should be able to find a position up on speed and should run well again. ROSIE POLLEN (1) was well beaten last time out in a race taken out by Arkuna. She draws well in this race and could be an improver. SELECTIONS: JAY TEE TYRON (8), THE HARRIS HAWK (9), FAVREAU (5), ROSIE POLLEN (1) SUGGESTED BET: JAY TEE TYRON (8) to win.

WHOS DELIGHT (6) looks a class above his rivals in this race having dropped considerably in grade. He ran fourth last time out behind Darin in a much stronger race at Albion Park. He may be able to work to the lead and should run well. SWEET AGENDA (4) has excellent early speed and may be able to zip across early before taking a sit WHOS DELIGHT (6). She was shuffled back early last time out and didn’t have the best of luck in a race taken out by Smarter Than You. TILLY JAYNE (3) raced without cover two starts ago when running a good third behind Great Achiever. She appears to draw reasonably in this race and should be close enough in the small field. REAL TIN TIN (1) has the perfect draw in this race and some early speed which should see him in a prominent position. He secured a good run leaders back two starts ago and couldn’t quite reel in Mullum Doc. SELECTIONS: WHOS DELIGHT (6), SWEET AGENDA (4), TILLY JAYNE (3), REAL TIN TIN (1) SUGGESTED BET: WHOS DELIGHT (6) to win.

LITTLE WHIPPET (2) led early last time out before handing over and was beaten in good time by Tellmeaboutit. He is likely to secure a good run again in this race from a great draw and should be right in the finish. PERFECT FEELING (3) led and over raced badly there last time out over the 2040 when fading late. He is likely to be much better suited stepping back to the 1780 in this race and if he could find the lead he would be hard to run down. WAR CLUB (5) secured a good run last time out and was able to sprint nicely to score a good win there. He is likely to be shuffled back early in this race and he should be running on well late. SAINT LOUIS BEAT (1) appeared to have every chance last time out when leading and fading late into fourth. He draws well again but may look to adopt different tactics in this race and could be better suited driven with a sit. SELECTIONS: LITTLE WHIPPET (2), PERFECT FEELING (3), WAR CLUB (5), SAINT LOUIS BEAT (1) SUGGESTED BET: LITTLE WHIPPET (2) to win.

CARLY PEREZ (3) was shuffled back last time out and was running on late behind Iam Hugo when first up from a spell there. She has previously shown good gate speed and if she could work to the lead in this race she would likely be hard to beat. SON OF XENA (5) was shuffled a long way back last start and finished it off strongly there in a race which became a dash home. He is likely to have derived a lot of benefit from the outing and can run well second up in this race. NOTIONS (9) secured a good run behind the leader two starts ago and was able to run second to smart filly Stripes. She backed that up with a good ninth in the QBRED Triad final last start and can run well again. MACKLEMORE CHEX (1) has been badly out of form and would need to improve significantly to be a hope in this race. He does draw well and has previously shown good ability. SELECTIONS: CARLY PEREZ (3), SON OF XENA (5), NOTIONS (9), MACKLEMORE CHEX (1) SUGGESTED BET: CARLY PEREZ (3) to win. OVERVIEW:TARA VICTORY (11) drops significantly back in grade from what she’s been facing at Melton in her seven runs this preparation. She won’t have the opportunity to use her gate speed from this draw, but based on her peak times, she’s significantly quicker than the majority of these. Earlier this season she won three from five when racing in similar grade, so if the tempo is suitable, she will be very strong late. IM WESLEY (10) is racing in career-best form this season, missing a place only four times in 16 starts. Those performances have all come with the opportunity to map well, and he now goes to the back row for the first time this season. However, there does appear to be a lot of speed off the front row, which may bring the backmarkers into it. HELLO POSSUMS (3) resumes from a break here off a couple of good trials, and her best preparation last time in saw her win two from three. She’s in the mix for the speed map, but there are a few others likely to have a look. MOMENTUM SHIFT (9) is another who finds more suitable company, having raced in strong races, often from bad draws. He can punch through off a solid tempo, and the last time he was in this ratings band he was a winner at Melton. As far as the minor money is concerned, it’s a long tail of chances, so play wide on the bottom line for exotics. BACK: TARA VICTORY (11)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:TARA VICTORY (11), IM WESLEY (10), HELLO POSSUMS (3), MOMENTUM SHIFT (9)

OVERVIEW:BULLETPROOF KID (6) has been flying this preparation and finds his most suitable race to grab a well-deserved win. When he’s been beaten in his past four runs, it has been by horses who have been competitive in quality races at Melton, and he’s gone down fighting and narrowly. He has very good gate speed to be assertive over the middle trip, and the claim of the in-form Ewa Justice, who gets on well with him, is a plus. MADAM REACTOR (5) will also run the gate, and her regular pattern is to take cover thereafter. She’s been racing honestly and likes this track, so will get her chance if that pattern eventuates. COOL STORY (10) has been racing well this season, winning two from six, and his two recent silver medals were also full of merit. He will be reliant on a solid tempo, but he’s in the mix. ANIMADO (11) has his first run since May without a trial, and although his numerical form looks plain, he has ability and loves the track. JULZ MARIE (1) and ELATED (4) have minor claims for exotics. BACK: BULLETPROOF KID (6)– 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:BULLETPROOF KID (6), MADAM REACTOR (5), COOL STORY (10), ANIMADO (11)

OVERVIEW:AGAINST THE BRIDLE (7) turned in a career-best run last time at his 100th start at Kilmore, running a peak mile rate and winning by 32 metres with an aggressive drive that saw him take the lead mid-race and run along. Surprisingly, that was only regular stable driver James Herbertson’s second drive on him. There may be a few looking for the top spot here, but none can put down similar times, and if he can back up that performance, he will be very hard to beat. I AM HARRO (8) can mix his form, but his best keeps him in the hunt here. He was a good winner five runs ago at Bendigo, where he came from back in the field. His last couple have been below par but he can bounce back against suitable opposition. ALDEBARAN MARCUS (9) has been sound in his past few runs and loomed up strongly last start before just peaking late. If the speed is on, it could help him work into it. Outside of those, it will come down to who gets the best run for the third/fourth spots, with KALARNEY PRINCE (6) and JESSICAS STORY (10) heading those chances. BACK: AGAINST THE BRIDLE (7)– 4 units (win) SELECTIONS:AGAINST THE BRIDLE (7), I AM HARRO (8), ALDEBARAN MARCUS (9), JESSICAS STORY (10)

OVERVIEW: OHHEMMJAY CRESCO (4) comes here fitter third-up and in suitable grade to produce his best over the short trip. He led up last time at Melton and was just outsprinted when fourth. Back to his home track, this opposition looks more suitable. Mark Pitt has had one drive on him for a win, which is another positive. TASTE IT (3) resumes here from a soft draw without a trial, but her form before going out for a break was sound enough for this grade. She gets the country’s top driver, which is a bonus. ARRAPS (6) turned in a nice effort last week when second, doing his best work late after the winner stole a march. His tactical speed gives him options from what appears a sticky draw. CLIVES GIRL (9) is always popular in the market in these races but has been a bit costly. This does, however, look to be another suitable assignment, so she is worth keeping safe. Minor chances go to MAJOR MAURIE (11), OLLY ODD POTTS (5), QUEENHIGH FLUSH (10) and ALCATRAZ GIRL (8), who are all capable of improvement with the right runs. BACK: OHHEMMJAY CRESCO (4)– 1.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:OHHEMMJAY CRESCO (4), TASTE IT (3), ARRAPS (6), CLIVES GIRL (9)

OVERVIEW: A very even race where luck in running may well prove the difference. FINAL BOW (4) was a strong winner here last week, albeit in an easier race, but she had to earn it from the outside of the front row, making ground from back in the field and putting down solid sectionals. She can afford a positive drive from the more favourable draw and map closer this time, and if she reproduces last week’s effort, she will take holding out. TREACHEROUSTIMES (3) is a quick beginner and will likely be used from the low gate, as he was a winner here two starts back when able to lead all the way and does have a liking for this track. TOMMYS LOOKOUT (2) was great here last week in an easier race, where despite sitting parked he was too strong for the opposition in a time that may be good enough at this level. TOBYS SHOUT (6) has now had two runs for the new stable, and his last start may be an indication he’s heading in the right direction. The draw is a little tricky, but he’s in the mix. WINGATE GUY (1) and CARUSO STAR (8) aren’t without a chance from their soft draws either. SELECTIONS: FINAL BOW (4), TREACHEROUSTIMES (3), TOMMYS LOOKOUT (2), TOBYS SHOUT (6)

OVERVIEW: A very high-quality race mixing 2yos and 3yos, and there’s some potentially smart talent engaged. STRAATHDALE (3) stepped out at a recent trial at Melton and looked very smart, quickly finding the lead before extending brilliantly with a final quarter of 26.4. He had four good trials prior to that also, so he’s had plenty of experience to attempt to lead all the way on debut here. INDULGEME (4) looked very smart in a recent trial here, where he took on older horses and let down with a powerful finish. This stable is striking at an incredible rate with its young debutants at the moment, and this one looks to have plenty of promise. MY ROCKING HORSE (1) ran into one who looks really smart when recording a good second on debut and had to do it tough last time when runner-up again. Both times were sharp, and the softer draw now is in her favour. KONSTAS (8) was terrific winning on debut but now goes to the back row and will be giving some smart types a start. And we haven’t even got to the 3yos AMADA VILLMA (5), TOUCH OF REALITY (6), PIASTRI (7) and THERESHEWAS (9), all of whom would have genuine claims under these conditions normally, but they’ve struck some pretty talented-looking opposition here. SELECTIONS: STRAATHDALE (3), INDULGEME (4), MY ROCKING HORSE (1), KONSTAS (8)

OVERVIEW: Looks an impossible race with limited form to get excited about. Wide in the Quaddie. SHEER ME (3) had her first run for the new stable at Ararat and didn’t have the cleanest passage there, getting checked back to last. She found the line okay, so from a more favourable draw and set-up, she can be in the mix. AXIS ANGEL (1) followed the peg line last start in a solid field and was okay to the line. The soft draw and Herbertson help his chances. DYGNALI (2) turned in a sound performance first-up from the same draw. With added fitness, she is open to improvement. MANFREDI (6) is her stablemate and comes here first-up. Last preparation he turned in a couple of okay runs in more challenging company than he meets here. SPOT THE DEVIL (5) changes stables, so could be open to improvement, and it may pay to monitor any betting moves. SANDEE CHEEKS (7) resumed with a third from a much softer draw last time, but the winner was much better than this opposition, so she will appreciate the class drop. SELECTIONS: SHEER ME (3), AXIS ANGEL (1)DYGNALI (2), MANFREDI (6)

OVERVIEW:AUSSIE JAY MAC (7) is a horse who, when he does everything right, shows he’s smart, as evidenced last time when he ran to the lead and recorded very good time for this grade. This draw isn’t as favourable, but he retains the same driver to push forward assertively, and even if he must sit parked, he can be hard to run down. MAMMALS REASON (5) is in excellent form this season, winning three of her past four. She may map to get a decent run, and although this is tougher, she’s right in it on what she’s been showing. ELIZAJANE (3) will no doubt be popular with punters, as she often is, particularly returning to a front-row draw where she can map well. Her last win came when she was able to lead. Those likely to settle close to the peg line in KNOW THE SCORE (1), HIGHVIEW HAMMER (2) and SWEET LOUANNE (8) are in contention to fight for the minor end of the prize. SELECTIONS:AUSSIE JAY MAC (7), MAMMALS REASON (5), ELIZAJANE (3), KNOW THE SCORE (1)

OVERVIEW:OUR MYSTERY BET (7) is crying out for another win and put in one of the runs of the night last week when sitting parked in decent time, only to be swooped late. He’s a horse who always runs at even fractions, which leaves him vulnerable late, but he’s going very well. MISS PIGGY WIGGY (4) returns to the front row and looks to get a good map here, with cover likely from out wide. She was finding the line well last time out and does tend to race well at this track. DOT BALL (5) has been in good form over the past month or so, winning two of her last three. She gets the type of set-up she likes, with good gate speed around her allowing her to sit off them and come with one run. SPUN SILVER (2) is a quick beginner and will be looking for the lead here, a position she races best in, as evidenced by her two wins this season from that position. She will take running down from there. SELECTIONS:OUR MYSTERY BET (7), MISS PIGGY WIGGY (4), DOT BALL (5), SPUN SILVER (2)

OVERVIEW:GUNFORHIRE (10) appears very well placed with the concession claim and back to a suitable grade after racing well up in class at headquarters. His performances there against quality opposition have been very good, including a strong finishing second behind a smart one, running strong sectionals to the line. He has a very good strike rate at this track, and there looks to be plenty of early speed for him to unleash his customary fast finish. STARZINHEREYES (6) is also coming back to a suitable grade, having bumped into a couple of smart ones running time in her past two at Melton. Prior to that, she was racing well in QLD and now returns to her former stable. She has blistering gate speed and can lead and give plenty of cheek. GOLD IN PARIS (3) steps up in grade, but she’s been racing very well, particularly when racing in front last time and giving a good kick. The map looks a little different here, but she deserves consideration. There are a few worth keeping safe for the minor prizes. EYENEEDTHAT (1) was poor first-up as favourite, but the soft draw and added fitness can bring improvement. ALLGOOD VINNIE (5) has speed, and his best form has him in the mix, RANGER RICK (8) is better than his recent form suggests. BACK: GUNFORHIRE (10) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: GUNFORHIRE (10), STARZINHEREYES (6), GOLD IN PARIS (3), RANGER RICK (8)

OVERVIEW: Many of these crossed paths last week at Ararat, but I’m steering away from that form and looking to the first-up MUFASA BART (6). He’s been well travelled over his racing career and lightly raced over the past couple of seasons, but when he’s found the racetrack, he’s shown ability. His last-start second at Wagga was very good, and he has been freshened and trialled well since. MISSMALACHITE (9) won the stronger of those two races from last week; however, she now goes to the back row after leading from an inside front-row draw last week. She’s going well enough for this grade. THE REGULATOR (8) is another whose slightly different form appeals, having won twice this season from seven attempts, although he has a tricky draw to overcome. DOCTOR GO JOH (7) was able to lead all the way from this gate last week and performed strongly. It’s just uncertain whether he will get the same favours this time around, but he must be kept safe. I wouldn’t be surprised if any of the others snuck into the minor money, as it will come down to luck in running. SELECTIONS: MUFASA BART (6), MISSMALACHITE (9), THE REGULATOR (8), DOCTOR GO JOH (7)

OVERVIEW: Terrific race with several runners possessing metropolitan-quality form. ALWAYS BE BLAKEY (5) was back to his best in winning last time at Melton, thanks to an exceptional drive from Herbertson, where he was able to lead and win. Furthermore, he looked a different horse racing on the pegs. He has the early speed to potentially do the same again here, and if he backs that performance up, he will be hard to beat. SWEET IDEAL (8) will be the beneficiary if the front line decides to overcook things, as she’s a fast mare with a very good turn of foot. She’s had a freshen-up since her win at Menangle, where she was way too good for her rivals when everything worked out perfectly. She’s classy and commands respect. ULTIMATE VINNIE (7) won’t know himself in this class, having consistently raced in FFA company. His most recent try at this level was two starts back, where he ran a good second. He’s a real threat, although the draw is tricky. ROADMASTER (6) is first-up in eight months, but he’s a very smart 6yo who has often raced against A-Grade opposition. He’s had two good trials leading into this, and whilst fitness is to come, he must be kept safe. The remaining unmentioned runners have claims, especially BOULEVARD BART (2), who is a progressive 4yo but takes on different gravy here. SELECTIONS: ALWAYS BE BLAKEY (5), SWEET IDEAL (8), ULTIMATE VINNIE (7), ROADMASTER (6)

TACTICALLY PERFECT (4) is a 3yo filly with the powerful Lee stable, resuming off a short break after showing great promise last preparation, winning in good time at Melton and recording a solid second behind a smart one. She’s had two trials leading into this, including last time out when she beat horses with much stronger exposed form. She’s not blessed with gate speed, so the map is a little uncertain, but her class gives her more upside than most. OUT TO STAY (9) was slightly better last time in what may stack up to be a decent form race when third. He has been costly this preparation but respect the stable to have him on an upward spiral. MUSELET (8) is never too far away, particularly from inside draws, which he gets here, and this looks significantly easier than what he’s been facing lately. He’ll need luck but is in the mix. EASTBRO KOZZY (7) ran well at Ararat last week from the inside draw in a stronger race. The draw is sticky here, but you have the right driver to overcome that. BACK: TACTICALLY PERFECT (4) – 4 units (win) SELECTIONS: TACTICALLY PERFECT (4), OUT TO STAY (9), MUSELET (8), EASTBRO KOZZY (7)

OVERVIEW: KYVALLEY MISTY (3) will no doubt have admirers based on the astute trainer/driver combination alone and her short SP profile, but she is an enigmatic type who’s hard to trust. However, this looks suitable. She was a winner last start when leading under mobile conditions in an easier race, so if she holds that form, she will take catching. OFF YOUR FACESKI (8) faces a task from the handicap and isn’t the most reliable beginner; however, his form this season is more positive than most here, winning 7 of 14. He has won under standing-start conditions, so it’s not a total risk having him high in calculations. In saying that, your confidence will grow dramatically if you see him trotting after 300m. JAKARTA (5) wasn’t at his best last time out, but his best form keeps him in calculations against this line-up. He was a winner back in July from a similar handicap, and if he brings that form, he’s right in it. BROWN EYED KATE (4) seems to be a trustworthy beginner away from the tapes, which is a big advantage in this line-up. She has been a little plain her past few, but her manners will carry her a long way. SELECTIONS: KYVALLEY MISTY (3), OFF YOUR FACESKI (8), JAKARTA (5), BROWN EYED KATE (4)

OVERVIEW: EMJAY JAZZ (2) ticks a few boxes in a race with limited form lines. She’s one of only two horses to win a race this season, drops out of a tougher race at Melton and boasts arguably the best strike rate. She’s a mare who possesses good early gate speed, and if she can control the race from the front, she can be hard to catch. YANKEE RAIN (3) has her second run for the new stable and was a little inconclusive from the tricky draw last week. Drawn to map better here, she’s worth another chance. THE BLAZINBOOTS (5) isn’t racing as well as he can; however, this race appears more suitable than what he’s been exposed to in four runs this preparation. JILLIBY KYMY LOU (4) is from the top stable but doesn’t possess the ability that most others from the camp bring to the races. She is a quick beginner, so potentially her map and a drop in class could open her up to improvement. PRESIDENTIALCHANGE (1) was good in winning last week, but he drew the pole to lead there, and this sets up very differently. SELECTIONS: EMJAY JAZZ (2), YANKEE RAIN (3), THE BLAZINBOOTS (5), JILLIBY KYMY LOU (4)

OVERVIEW: Tricky affair, mixing 2yo and 3yo form along with trials that are a little difficult to line up against the exposed race form. Starting with the trials, JILLIBY STRANGER (1) is a 2yo who found the line best in a recent Terang outing, while stablemate and 3yo KEAYANG MARICRUZ (2) went across the line with MIDNIGHT FEAST (3). The one to take out of the trial was JILLIBY STRANGER (1). Of those with exposed form, DEVERAUX (4) and MIKI SHADOW (5) are both last-start winners, with DEVERAUX (4) the more impressive of the pair, both to the eye and on the clock. BANGBANG BOBBIE (7) has had market respect at his two starts but probably needs to improve on what he’s shown so far. Looking at how the map may play out, JILLIBY STRANGER (1) showed reasonable speed and may look to hold up from that draw, whilst the others may all look to duck to the peg line. I’ll lean to DEVERAUX (4) on the strength of the time he’s already recorded under race conditions, which these may struggle to match. SELECTIONS: DEVERAUX (4), JILLIBY STRANGER (1), MIKI SHADOW (5), KEAYANG MARICRUZ (2)

OVERVIEW: KEAYANG GYPSY (8) was backed off the map last start at Melton but was costly to punters, galloping away from the mobile and losing all chance. Her two runs prior, back from a break, were very good, winning first-up and then brave second-up when forced to work on a decent pace. Standing-start conditions have been favourable for her in the past, winning twice from six attempts. With a safe beginning, her form is good enough to overhaul these despite the handicap. KEAYANG LAVITA (5) has plenty of ability, but she’s been her own worst enemy, either underperforming or breaking in running, mostly in quality grade at Melton this season. You must go back to November last year for her last win, and prior to that she was building a nice record. She’s trialled well leading into this, and it’s only a matter of time before she cleans up her act and bounces back. KEAYANG TWEETYBIRD (3) doesn’t have the ability of her two stablemates, but unfortunately, she too has been a bit wayward with her manners. When she gets it right, she’s pretty good, so is worth keeping safe. EL CONQUEROR (6) led and had every hope last start, but he does seem to like the tapes, so if the others wipe themselves out, his manners can carry him a long way. BACK: KEAYANG GYPSY (8) – 3.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: KEAYANG GYPSY (8), KEAYANG LAVITA (5), KEAYANG TWEETYBIRD (3), EL CONQUEROR (6)
